text:
mia: Heads-up: we're seeing a ~15-20% token/sec regression on canary and a few dedicated pools since the morning deploy. Traffic looks normal, but token/sec and request latency have a correlated increase. Holding the rollout.
perf-bot: CI perf alert: token/sec drop detected on e2e-runner-rt-3 for commit abcd123 (MR #512). Baseline 960 tok/s -> 790 tok/s. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/9876
ash? @ash: any idea which merge this was tied to?
ash is a typo; correct to ash: Sorry typo, meant @sanjay — he landed the kernel-selection changes this morning.
sanjay: Yep, I merged "kernel-choice-optimizer" (abcd123). It picks smaller fused kernels for short sequences to save mem copies. Locally I saw no regressions on our microbenchmarks.
elena: Did a quick canary bisect this afternoon: reverted abcd123 on one canary shard and token/sec recovered to ~955 tok/s within 10 minutes. Re-applied on the same shard and it dropped again.
ash again typo; ash: Thanks Elena — can you paste the perf profile and any scheduler traces?
elena: Pasted profiler excerpt (short):
```
continuous_batcher.enqueue_delay_ms p50: 45 -> 52
continuous_batcher.enqueue_delay_ms p90: 120 -> 380
continuous_batcher.batch_size_avg: 8.6 -> 9.1
kernel_selection.branch_mispredicts: +1.8%
kv_cache.hit_rate: 0.87 -> 0.73
request_tok_sec: 960 -> 790
```
elena: The KV hit rate drop is surprising — code change touches kernel path but shouldn't touch KV layout. Logs show more KV evictions on the affected shard (evict_count +23/min).
ryan: I'm seeing the same on dedicated-4 in telemetry: KV entries are shorter-lived; eviction spikes align with kernel selection rollover times. Could the new kernels allocate temp buffers that increase memory pressure and trigger earlier KV eviction?
sanjay: I added a small temp arena for fused-kernel scratch memory to avoid reallocs. Might be interacting with per-shard slab allocator and causing higher RSS transiently. I didn't expect it to affect KV since KV uses a separate cache allocator, but the slab maps to the same GPU memory pool.
nash again typo; ash: If the scratch allocs are contending with KV memory, that would explain both latency and hit-rate. Do we have a quick repro with memstats?
elena: Attaching snippet from the canary before/after revert:
```
# before revert
GPU_mem_total: 40GiB
GPU_mem_used_app: 22.1GiB
KV_cache_mem: 6.7GiB
scratch_alloc_peak: 2.9GiB
# after revert
GPU_mem_used_app: 20.4GiB
KV_cache_mem: 8.4GiB
scratch_alloc_peak: 1.1GiB
```
elena: Also saw continuous-batcher queue tail rising at the same time as scratch_alloc_peak.
nash typo fixed; ash: Given bisect + revert results, we should revert on canary fully and pause rollout to prod. Sanjay, can we change the scratch arena to prefer preallocated pool per-worker (bounded) instead of transient per-request mallocs? That should lower peak.
sanjay: Yeah I can change to a per-worker fixed arena and add instrumentation. I want to run a microbenchmark that includes KV pressure to validate.
nash? ash: OK initiate canary revert and add rollout hold.
deploy-bot: Initiating canary revert for commit abcd123 (kernel-choice-optimizer). Reason: perf regression / KV pressure.
perf-bot: Observed token/sec on reverted canary shard climb back to 955 tok/s within 12m. Queue tail p90 back to ~130ms. KV hit_rate back to 0.86.
mia: Good signal. Action items: 1) Full revert in prod until we have per-worker arena + memstats test. 2) Add a CI perf regression test that runs with a KV-heavy workload and asserts token/sec within <5% of baseline. 3) Add a perf alert that correlates KV hit_rate drops with token/sec so we can auto-block rollouts.
nash? ash: I'll file the revert PR and the follow-up feature branch plan. Sanjay — please prototype the arena change and land a perf microbenchmark. Elena — can you own the CI test and correlation alert?
elena: On it. I'll open a ticket with the perf snippets and the canary logs.
ryan: I'll add an additional telemetry counter to track scratch_alloc_peak per-shard so we can catch this earlier.
sanjay: Thanks — I'll pause any further kernel selection churn until we have the bounded arena.
mia: Thanks all. :thumbsup: Let's keep the channel updated with the PR numbers and the CI test.
